overview: This bill renews through 2030 the federal law behind the Integrated Ocean Observing System, a national network of buoys, sensors and data systems run with regional partners that tracks ocean and coastal conditions used for weather forecasts, shipping safety and coastal management. It extends the system's funding authorization for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 and requires that each regional coastal observing system in existence on January 1, 2025, receive at least 7.5 percent of the money appropriated, apart from disaster relief funds. It moves oversight from a former interagency council to the Ocean Policy Committee, adds meteorological observations and data management and cyber infrastructure to the system's purposes, and removes a reference to global climate change. Yearly reports to Congress would also need to evaluate how the system's data affected forecast accuracy for major storms. As of May 11, 2026, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate calendar.
for: Supporters say ocean and coastal data are essential for accurate storm forecasts, safe navigation and coastal planning, and guaranteeing funds to each regional system keeps that network stable.
against: Critics say locking in a minimum share for each existing regional system limits flexibility to direct money where it is most needed, and removing the reference to climate change narrows the system's stated purpose.
